subject: Wrapped selections now delete completely, the three Backspace shortcuts edit word line or all input, and selected letters fade in their normal colour for 650ms.
reader: Parker, who reported multiline selection deletion failing in the native test window and requested these exact keys, help translations and a more visible 650ms erasure trail.

sections.heading: Delete long terminal selections
sections.text:
In Terminal Delight, long typed commands can continue onto a second or third screen row. Selecting those rows and pressing Backspace now removes the selected text. The same build adds your word, line and whole-input shortcuts, with a brighter 650 ms fade for erased letters. 

650 ms 
Minimum erasure fade, with more light remaining later in the fade. Ordinary replacements still start at 220 ms. Zero turns both off.

sections.heading: Backspace takes the whole selection
sections.text:
The old code accepted selections on only one row. A real mouse-drag test reproduced your failure: the selected passage stayed, and one character at the caret disappeared. The new range follows the wrapped input. These native captures exercise the keyboard path in a real Bash editor.

The cursor then moves left, with acknowledgement at 101 ms; the lingering capture spans 507–631 ms after the deletion gesture. The neighboring pane stays pixel-identical. sections.heading: Three shortcuts choose how much to erase
sections.text:
The shortcuts choose text from the caret position in the focused editor. Deleting a line takes both sides of the caret and includes its soft wraps. Clearing input also takes the other lines in a multiline draft. It keeps terminal history and sends no Enter or interrupt. | 
 | Shortcut | Action 
 | Shift+Backspace | Delete the previous word. 
 | Ctrl+Shift+Backspace | Delete the entire current line. 
 | Ctrl+Shift+Alt+Backspace | Clear the entire editable input. 
 02 · THREE REAL INPUT LINES 
 Figure 2. Line deletion preserves the other two lines; whole-input deletion clears all three. Drawn from exact Readline buffer receipts after real keyboard events. The workbench composer applies the same distinction locally, with undo. Terminal shortcuts use Readline-compatible editing; arbitrary full-screen editors keep their own keys. measured

sections.heading: The updated window is ready to try
sections.text:
Your separate instance is open on workspace 4 , in INPUT EDITING · 650 ms . The fresh Standard and Intrusive panes keep your current picture settings. All six earlier shells, including unfinished input, are preserved in the other tabs. 
Type or paste a long command, select across a wrap with the mouse or Shift+Arrow, and press Backspace. Try the three shortcuts at the beginning, middle and end of your input. The existing demonstration command uses the longer fade: 
afterglow-demo 

 Trail strength 
The erased letters now retain their normal colour and fade linearly over at least 650 ms. Leave a note here after trying it if the remaining light still needs adjustment. 

 Verification and source 
 2,621 default-core tests and 2,568 fallback-core tests passed , with 10 ignored in each. Both strict Clippy gates, format, diff check and the locked release build passed. Tests cover real mouse and keyboard selection across wraps, literal-newline selection with a preserved suffix, all three shortcuts, composer undo, text-field key ownership and clean retained colours. 
The clean glyph snapshot excludes TD selection and cursor overlays while preserving the program's own colours and inversion. It uses the same painted coordinates as the live grid. The erasure trail uses a linear fade and expires at 650 ms in exact-clock tests. Ordinary replacement retains its earlier curve and default. Native zero-disabled captures match exactly. The observed capture interval is not a GPU frame deadline. 
The real terminal checks use isolated Bash fixtures and do not type into existing user shells. The tested executable is the one running in the refreshed window. GPU frame cost, including the additional cached clean styles, remains unmeasured qualification work . 
Evidence: native inputs and timing · old-build reproduction · pixel comparisons · test totals · preserved shell identities .
